input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s this number—555-123-2002—that I’m having trouble with. That’s the only phone I use. What should I do next?

Looking at the top of my phone, it says “No Signal” and I don’t see any bars. There’s also something about data being disabled, I think. I don’t see an airplane icon, though. What does this mean? Is that bad?
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. Is that the problem? What should I do now?

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in, just like you said. Now, at the top of my phone, I see a few bars (though it says “Poor”), and it says “2G.” But it still says data is disabled. Is this any better? What should I do next?

Okay, I turned on the mobile data. Now I see a little icon that looks like a phone, and it still says “2G” with a poor signal. Is that good enough, or do I need to do something else? I’m not sure if this will let me send a picture message yet.

I changed the setting to “4G/5G preferred” like you said. Now at the top, it says “5G” and the signal looks excellent. The mobile data icon is still there too. Is this what we want? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message—it just doesn’t send. This is getting a bit frustrating. What else can I do?

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I selected it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. It just won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending a picture message again? Or do you want me to check the messaging app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next?

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has permission for storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Is that a problem? Should I try to add the SMS permission, or is there something else I should do?

I was able to add the SMS permission for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. It just won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture message) issue. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any service or data issues that might be affecting your ability to send MMS. 

Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD), or
- Your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

Thank you for providing your information. I’ll help you troubleshoot your MMS issue.

To get started, could you please confirm if you’re having trouble sending picture messages from the phone number 555-123-2002, or is it a different line on your account? If it’s a different number, please let me know which one.

Once confirmed, I’ll guide you through some quick checks on your device to identify the cause of the problem.
Yes, it’s this number—555-123-2002—that I’m having trouble with. That’s the only phone I use. What should I do next?

Thank you for confirming. Let’s start by checking a few things on your phone to diagnose the MMS issue.

Please follow these steps on your device and let me know the results:

1. Check your phone’s status bar (the area at the top of your screen) and let me know:
   - Do you see any signal bars, or does it say “No Signal”?
   - Is there an airplane icon (✈️) showing?
   - Do you see “4G”, “5G”, or any network type indicator?
   - Is there a mobile data icon (📱) or does it show “Data Disabled”?

This information will help me determine if there’s a service or data issue affecting your ability to send MMS.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Looking at the top of my phone, it says “No Signal” and I don’t see any bars. There’s also something about data being disabled, I think. I don’t see an airplane icon, though. What does this mean? Is that bad?

Thank you for checking. Seeing “No Signal” and data being disabled means your phone currently doesn’t have cellular service or mobile data, which are both required to send MMS (picture messages). This is likely the reason your MMS messages aren’t going through.

Let’s try to restore your service. First, we should check the status of your SIM card, as issues with the SIM can cause a loss of signal.

On your phone, please check your SIM card status and let me know:
- Does your phone say the SIM is missing, locked, or active?

If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know what you see regarding the SIM card in your phone’s settings or notifications.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. Is that the problem? What should I do now?

Yes, if your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, that is likely the cause of your “No Signal” and inability to send MMS. The SIM card is required for your phone to connect to the cellular network.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card from its slot.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly seated.
4. Power your phone back on.

After you’ve done this, check if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you have signal bars. Let me know what you see after reseating the SIM card.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in, just like you said. Now, at the top of my phone, I see a few bars (though it says “Poor”), and it says “2G.” But it still says data is disabled. Is this any better? What should I do next?

Great job reseating the SIM card! Now that your phone detects the SIM and you have some signal, we’re making progress. However, “2G” is a very slow network and may not support MMS, and data being disabled will also prevent MMS from working.

Let’s do the following next steps:

1. Enable mobile data on your phone. Please turn on your mobile data connection in your phone’s settings.
2. After enabling data, check if you see a mobile data icon (like 📱) and if the network changes from “2G” to something faster (like “4G” or “5G”).

Once you’ve done this, let me know:
- If mobile data is now enabled,
- What network type you see (2G, 3G, 4G, or 5G).

This will help us determine if you’re ready to try sending an MMS again.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned on the mobile data. Now I see a little icon that looks like a phone, and it still says “2G” with a poor signal. Is that good enough, or do I need to do something else? I’m not sure if this will let me send a picture message yet.

Thank you for the update. While you now have mobile data enabled, being on a “2G” network with a poor signal is usually not sufficient for sending MMS (picture messages). MMS typically requires at least a 3G, 4G, or 5G connection.

Let’s try to improve your network connection by changing your phone’s network mode preference to allow faster networks (like 4G or 5G), if available in your area.

Please go to your phone’s network settings and set the preferred network mode to “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only” if that’s an option. After changing this setting, check if your phone connects to a faster network (look for “4G” or “5G” at the top of your screen).

Let me know what network type you see after making this change. If you need help finding this setting, let me know your phone model and I can guide you further.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I changed the setting to “4G/5G preferred” like you said. Now at the top, it says “5G” and the signal looks excellent. The mobile data icon is still there too. Is this what we want? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?

That’s excellent progress! Now that your phone shows “5G” with an excellent signal and mobile data is enabled, your device should be able to send MMS (picture messages).

Please try sending a picture message now. If it goes through successfully, your issue is resolved. If you still have trouble sending MMS, let me know what happens (any error messages or if it just doesn’t send), and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message—it just doesn’t send. This is getting a bit frustrating. What else can I do?

Thank you for your patience. Since you now have a strong 5G signal and mobile data enabled, but MMS still isn’t working, the next most common cause is an issue with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Here’s what you should do next:
1. Go to your phone’s mobile network settings and look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
2. Check if there’s an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” Please select this option to reset your APN settings to the carrier defaults.
3. After resetting the APN, restart (reboot) your phone.

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have trouble sending MMS.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I selected it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?

Rest assured, restarting (rebooting) your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. A reboot simply turns your phone off and back on, refreshing its system and applying any new settings (like the APN reset).

You will not lose any important information by restarting your device. Once you’ve rebooted, your phone will keep all your photos, messages, apps, and contacts just as they were.

Please go ahead and restart your phone. After it powers back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. It just won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

Thank you for following all the steps so far. I understand this is frustrating, but there are still a few more things we can check to resolve your MMS issue.

Let’s try the following:

1. Check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Please go to your phone’s settings and see if Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON. If it is, please turn it OFF and try sending a picture message again.

2. If that doesn’t help, we should also check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS. Specifically, it needs permission to access storage and SMS. Please check your app permissions for your messaging app and ensure both “storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

Please let me know:
- If Wi-Fi Calling was ON and if turning it OFF helped,
- If your messaging app has the correct permissions.

If you need help finding these settings, let me know your phone model and I can guide you step by step.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending a picture message again? Or do you want me to check the messaging app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

Please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling first, then try sending a picture message again. Sometimes, simply disabling Wi-Fi Calling resolves MMS issues.

If the picture message still doesn’t send after turning off Wi-Fi Calling, let me know, and we’ll move on to checking your messaging app permissions next.

Let me know what happens after you try sending the MMS with Wi-Fi Calling turned off.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next?

Thank you for trying that step. Next, let’s check your messaging app’s permissions to ensure it has access to storage and SMS, which are required for sending MMS.

Please do the following:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find “Apps” or “Applications,” then select your messaging app.
3. Tap on “Permissions.”
4. Make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled for your messaging app.

After you’ve checked and, if needed, enabled these permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still can’t send MMS.
App 'messaging' has permission for: storage, phone.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has permission for storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Is that a problem? Should I try to add the SMS permission, or is there something else I should do?

Yes, your messaging app needs SMS permission to send and receive text and picture messages (MMS). If SMS permission is not enabled or not listed, that could be the reason you’re unable to send MMS.

Please try to add or enable the SMS permission for your messaging app:
- In your app permissions settings, look for “SMS” or “Messages.”
- If you see it, enable or allow this permission for your messaging app.

If you don’t see an option for SMS permission, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can guide you on how to find or enable it.

Once you’ve enabled SMS permission, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works.

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I was able to add the SMS permission for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. It just won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. Since you have a strong signal, mobile data enabled, correct network mode, APN settings reset, Wi-Fi Calling off, and all necessary app permissions granted, but MMS still isn’t working, we’ve covered all the standard troubleshooting steps.

At this point, your issue may require more advanced technical support. I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate further and provide specialized assistance.

You are being transferred to a human agent. Please hold on.
